content.text: The minimal reproduction confirms it on current HEAD with an unrelated package (`npm:cowsay@1.6.0`): the second and third `mise exec` both reinstall-check it, print `already installed`, then warn `missing`, while `mise ls` says installed/active and `mise which` resolves it. The key clue is that merely enabling lockfile creation in the project changes the global tool’s satisfaction test, even though `mise lock` explicitly says global tools are outside that project lock.

content.text:
Confirmed: [Discussion #13184](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13184) reports a real regression introduced by [PR #13131](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13131) in v2026.9.7. There are currently no replies.

I reproduced it on current `main` with an isolated environment and `npm:cowsay@1.6.0`:

```text
mise ⇢ npm:cowsay@1.6.0 · already installed
mise WARN  missing: npm:cowsay@1.6.0
1.6.0
```

Every subsequent `mise exec` repeats the install check and warning, while `mise ls` reports `installed: true, active: true` and `mise which` resolves the executable correctly.

The root cause is [src/backend/npm.rs:501](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/98cf/mise/src/backend/npm.rs:501). An npm request without an attached aube graph is declared unsatisfied whenever the merged `Settings` says lockfile creation is enabled:

```rust
!tv.resolved_from_lockfile() && Settings::get().lockfile_creation_enabled()
```

A project’s `lockfile = true` enters that merged setting, even when the npm request belongs to the global config. This contradicts the lockfile ownership rules in [src/lockfile.rs:2508](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/98cf/mise/src/lockfile.rs:2508), which explicitly avoid automatically creating global lockfiles.

Running `mise lock --global` made the reproduction immediately silent, confirming that the missing owner-specific graph is the distinction—not the physical installation.

The fix should make the “graph required” decision relative to the request’s owning lockfile rather than the merged project setting. Care is needed to preserve:

- Existing revision-2 lockfiles that need graphs.
- Project configs explicitly opting into automatic lockfile creation.
- The legacy `MISE_LOCKFILE=1` behavior.
- Global lockfiles remaining opt-in through `mise lock --global`.

An e2e regression test should install a global-only npm tool, enable lockfiles in a separate project, and assert repeated `mise exec` and `mise install --dry-run` remain satisfied. The existing npm graph tests cover project tools but not this global/project ownership boundary.

No repository changes or GitHub replies were made.
make a pr, post a reply
I’ll turn the confirmed ownership bug into a focused regression fix, run the npm/lockfile checks, open a review-ready PR, then re-read the discussion immediately before posting the public reply.

content.text: The safest focused change is to align npm’s graph requirement with the existing lockfile creation boundary: project `lockfile = true` may create project locks, but it must not impose a graph on a request owned by the global config. I’m applying that condition in both the pre-install and satisfaction paths and adding an end-to-end test for the exact global/project split.
